MerchantCost.rationale: RelicModel.MerchantCost is virtual and the Fake Merchant's knock-offs all pin 50; relics/base.py:111-117 reads merchant_cost_override first and falls back to _MERCHANT_COST_BY_RARITY (relics/base.py:54-62), whose table is value-for-value the source's switch (RelicModel.cs:304-315, checked: Common 175 / Uncommon 225 / Rare 275 / Shop 200 / Ancient, Starter, Event 999999999). No AscensionHelper branch anywhere, so 50 is the pinned non-ascension price. Rule 7: RelicModel.cs and relics/base.py are not hashed by this record.

BeforeCombatStart.rationale: FakeSneckoEye.cs:31-34 calls the private ApplyPower (lines 36-40), which is `PowerCmd.Apply<ConfusedPower>(new ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext(), Owner.Creature, 1m, Owner.Creature, null)` -- amount 1, applier = the owner's own creature, cardSource null. fake_snecko_eye.py:21-23 is PowerCmd.apply(hooks, player, ConfusedPower, 1, applier=self.combat.player), matching the amount and the applier and leaving the card None. No AscensionHelper branch in the file. EXECUTED (py tools/audit/relic_probes_b05.py snecko-confused): combat starts with confused=1 and applier is the player, and the opening hand's costs come out randomized (e.g. [2, 1, 1, 2, 1] instead of the deck's fixed 1s). The sim's on_combat_start is the BeforeCombatStart slot (executed order, py tools/audit/relic_probes.py turn-order), so the hook mapping is right as well as the arguments.

AfterObtained.maps_to: no counterpart -- the sim's port defines only on_combat_start
AfterObtained.issue: MECHANISM: FakeSneckoEye.cs:23-29 applies the Confused power immediately when the relic is picked up if `CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress`, so a Fake Snecko Eye obtained mid-combat confuses you for the rest of that fight. The sim implements no after_obtained at all, so a mid-combat pickup does nothing until the next combat. EXECUTED (py tools/audit/relic_probes_b05.py snecko-confused): the port has no after_obtained override, and run.add_relic('fake_snecko_eye') applies no power. DORMANT, and the concrete unported thing is the same one relic/belt_buckle's AfterObtained entry names: the sim grants relics through RunState.add_relic between rooms (run.py:546-553), so a mid-combat pickup needs ported content that hands out a relic inside a fight, a shape the sim does not currently reach. Recorded as a gap rather than a waiver because 'the sim has no path here' is today's content and not the divergence's shape -- binding rule 1, and the same verdict relic/belt_buckle gives the identical mechanism (binding rule 3). Rule 7: run.py is unhashed here.

guards.what: N1 (PROMPT.md bug class 18): SetTestEnergyCostOverride / ApplyTestEnergyCostOverrideToPower (FakeSneckoEye.cs:42-60) are a TestMode-only surface, and the port correctly drops them
guards.rationale: SetTestEnergyCostOverride opens with TestMode.AssertOn() (FakeSneckoEye.cs:44), so it throws outside a test run, and ApplyTestEnergyCostOverrideToPower is a no-op whenever _testEnergyCostOverride is its initial -1 (FakeSneckoEye.cs:15, 52) -- which it always is in the shipping game, because the only writer is the AssertOn-guarded setter. So both calls to it (lines 39, 47) are dead in shipping. EXECUTED: the sim's relic has no set_test_energy_cost_override attribute. Waived as test scaffolding rather than filed as a dormant gap, on the same basis as the batch-1 power.IsVisible finding and PROMPT.md class 18's note that TestMode.TurnOnInternal has no caller under src/: this is dead code in the C# source itself, not unported content. Contrast relic/calling_bell, which ported the TestMode ARM of a two-arm body and is a live gap -- FakeSneckoEye has no such fork, only an extra test entry point, and the port took the right side of it.

guards.what: N2: the applier is the owner's own creature (FakeSneckoEye.cs:38), unlike the null applier most relics pass
guards.rationale: Checked deliberately because a non-null applier is what relic/unsettling_lamp's doubling keys on (`applier is self.player`, and Confused IS a Debuff). The Lamp cannot double this application for two independent reasons, both structural: the Lamp bails unless a card is mid-play (its _in_flight is None at combat start) and it bails when the target is the player. The sim passes the same non-null applier as the source, so the two codebases are exposed to the same interaction surface -- which is the point of recording it. Rule 7: relics/unsettling_lamp.py is unhashed here.

guards.what: N3: the relic grants NO extra card draw, where the real Snecko Eye draws 2 more
guards.rationale: FakeSneckoEye.cs has no ModifyHandDraw override anywhere in the file -- all downside, no upside, which is the knock-off's joke -- and the sim's port likewise defines no modify_hand_draw. Verified by reading the C# file in full; recorded because an auditor pattern-matching on the real Snecko Eye would expect a draw modifier and mistake its absence for a dropped hook.

guards.what: N4: `new ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext()` (FakeSneckoEye.cs:38) and the Confused ExtraHoverTips (line 21)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / VfxCmd / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, the damage/heal numbers and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim. ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext is multiplayer plumbing -- a choice context that throws if a player choice is required -- noted in the mapping rather than verdicted as a divergence, per the shared contract's scope section.
